<explanation>
Based on the file structure and README for nebula-sync, here’s a detailed explanation of how to create a system design diagram and architectural overview tailored to this project:

1. Project Type and Purpose:
   • This is a Go-based CLI tool (that can also run in a Docker container) designed to synchronize the configuration of a primary Pi-hole instance with one or more replica instances.
   • The README highlights two main synchronization modes ("Full sync" via Teleporter and "Selective sync"). It also shows that the tool can be scheduled via cron and run in containerized environments.
   
2. Analyze the File Structure:
   • Top-Level Directories/Files:
     - cmd: Contains the main entry points (root.go, run.go) where command-line parsing and the program startup happen.
     - internal: Holds the core business logic:
         ▪ config: Reads and validates environment variables and configuration settings.
         ▪ log: Handles logging across the application.
         ▪ pihole: Encapsulates interactions with Pi-hole’s API including data model definitions.
         ▪ service: Likely acts as an orchestrator for the overall synchronization logic.
         ▪ sync: Contains modules for the synchronization process with subdivisions for “full”, “selective”, “retry” and filtering logic.
         ▪ mocks: Contains mocks for Pi-hole and sync components for testing purposes.
     - e2e, testdata: For end-to-end and other tests.
     - version: Provides versioning information.
     - Others: GitHub workflows, Dockerfile, and related build/release configurations.
   
3. Guidelines for Creating the Diagram:
   a. Identify the Main Components:
      - Command Line Interface: The cmd package (cmd/root.go, cmd/run.go) starts the application.
      - Configuration Module: internal/config loads environment variables and configuration files.
      - Logging Module: internal/log to provide insight into the system’s operation.
      - Service Component: internal/service coordinates the synchronization process.
      - Pi-hole API Client: internal/pihole — this module actually communicates with the primary Pi-hole and replicas, processing models defined in internal/pihole/model.
      - Synchronization Modules: internal/sync containing various strategies (full sync, selective sync, retry logic, and filtering) to control how configuration is transmitted.
   b. Relationships and Interactions:
      - The application begins execution in main.go / cmd/run.go, which initializes the configuration and logger.
      - The configuration module reads and validates the environment variables (like PRIMARY, REPLICAS, FULL_SYNC, CRON, etc.) that control behavior.
      - The service layer (internal/service) uses the loaded configuration to decide which synchronization method (from internal/sync) to activate.
      - The synchronization modules then make use of the Pi-hole client (internal/pihole) to export/import configuration data from the primary instance and push it to the replicas.
      - Depending on flags (e.g., FULL_SYNC versus selective items), the internal/sync submodules (full, selective, retry) drive different data flows.
   c. Architectural Patterns/Design Principles:
      - Modular design: Separation of concerns is clear in the package structure (e.g., config, logging, service, pihole client, sync strategies).
      - Dependency separation: The service layer abstracts underlying client interactions, making it easier to swap out components (as seen with mocks for testing).
      - Testability: Presence of unit tests in most directories (e.g., config_test.go, client_test.go) and end-to-end tests in the e2e directory.
   d. Relevant Technologies:
      - Go as the programming language.
      - Docker for containerization (Dockerfile, docker-compose examples in README).
      - GitHub Actions for CI/CD (workflows in .github/workflows).
      - Cron scheduling is supported via configuration.
   
4. Diagram Tailoring (Based on Project Type – CLI Tool with API Integration):
   - Emphasize the clear separation between configuration initialization, business logic handling (service and sync), and external interactions (Pi-hole API client).
   - Highlight how the synchronization is triggered from the command-line entry point, with conditional branches based on FULL_SYNC or selective sync modes.
   - Include an external box representing the Pi-hole instances (one primary, multiple replicas), and draw arrows showing the data flow from the sync logic to these external systems.
   - Optionally, illustrate Docker as a deployment container that wraps the whole service.
   
5. Diagram Elements to Include:
   - Clearly label each component (e.g., “CLI (cmd)”, “Configuration Manager (internal/config)”, “Logging (internal/log)”, “Sync Service (internal/service)”, “Sync Modules (internal/sync: full, selective, retry)”, “Pi-hole Client (internal/pihole)”, “Primary Pi-hole”, “Replica Pi-hole(s)”).
   - Use directional arrows to indicate data flow:
       ▪ From CLI → Config and Logger initialization.
       ▪ From Config → Service (to set sync mode and parameters).
       ▪ From Service → Pi-hole Client (to perform the actual API calls).
       ▪ Return flows (e.g., responses, error handling) should also be indicated.
   - Use distinct colors or shapes to differentiate core modules (e.g., service components, external API clients, and external systems such as the Pi-hole primary/replicas).
   - Incorporate annotations related to the environment configuration (e.g., environment variables that affect behavior).
   
6. Step-by-Step Instructions for the Principal Software Engineer:
   • Begin with a high-level box representing the entire nebula-sync application.
   • Draw a starting node labeled “CLI” which maps to main.go and cmd/run.go.
   • Create linked boxes for “Configuration Manager” and “Logger”, showing that CLI initializes these.
   • Connect these to a central “Sync Service” box which controls the synchronization workflow.
   • Break “Sync Service” into sub-components:
         – “Full Sync Module” (from internal/sync/full)
         – “Selective Sync Module” (from internal/sync/selective)
         – “Retry/Resilience Module” (from internal/sync/retry)
         – “Filters” (from internal/sync/filter)
   • From the “Sync Service”, draw arrows to a “Pi-hole API Client” box, which manages both the primary (exporting data) and the replicas (importing data).
   • Surround or link external boxes representing “Primary Pi-hole” and “Replica Pi-hole(s)” with bi-directional arrows indicating API interactions.
   • Optionally, include a container or additional structure to illustrate that the whole application can be deployed in a Docker container and run on cron schedules.
   • Clearly label each arrow with what type of data or control signal is passed (for example, “Sync commands”, “API calls”, “Configuration data”).
   • Use color coding: maybe a unique color for configuration and initialization components, another for service logic, and a third for external integration (Pi-hole systems).
   
By following these instructions, the final system design diagram will clearly capture the essential architectural elements of nebula-sync, displaying how configuration, service orchestration, synchronization strategies, and external API interactions fit together to implement the project’s core functionality.
</explanation>
